assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, the active truncated peptides, insulinotropic and satiety actions) led to incretin therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and show cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery is original, clear and has very large lasting impact on human health.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across basic discovery (Holst, Mojsov, Habener-type work), mechanistic and translational biology (Drucker) and drug development (Knudsen). A trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov captures the physiological discovery, but the contribution of Mojsov versus others and the place of drug-development scientists are contested in my recollection.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of replication, large randomized outcome trials and global clinical use. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Exact allocation of credit for identifying the biologically active GLP-1 peptides is disputed and I have not verified it independently.
Whether a prize should honour drug development (Knudsen) rather than physiology is a judgement call.
Habener is not on the supplied credited names, so the physiological discovery may be incompletely represented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as the dominant driver of cytokine cascades in synovial tissue and the clinical demonstration that anti-TNF antibodies treat rheumatoid arthritis established cytokine blockade as a therapeutic principle, extended to Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. Clear, original bench-to-bedside discovery with enormous lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the rheumatoid synovium cytokine work and first clinical trials, a natural two-person configuration. Others (e.g. TNF cloning and antibody engineering groups) contributed to the molecular tools, so there is some risk of disputed priority.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than 25 years of use, multiple independent drugs and confirmation across diseases. Recognition is timely and long awaited.
uncertainties: Priority relative to those who cloned TNF or developed the antibodies is not fully resolved in the supplied information.
Whether the committee wishes to recognize the cytokine concept, the antibody engineering, or both.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a new class of living drug that built on adoptive cell therapy. High originality and clear clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed key early CAR design (costimulation), June the first clinical successes and clinical programme, Rosenberg adoptive T-cell and early gene-engineered cell therapy. Earlier CAR concept work (Eshhar) is not in the supplied names, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature with approved products and long follow-up showing cures in some patients, though toxicity, solid tumour limits and durability questions persist.
uncertainties: Eshhar and other originators of the chimeric receptor concept are absent from the credited names.
Long-term outcomes and secondary malignancy risk are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin discovery and its use to control genetically defined neurons with light created a method that has reshaped neuroscience and is used across physiology. Original, clear and enormously influential, though its medical impact is mainly as a research tool.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is difficult: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann characterized channelrhodopsin, Boyden and Deisseroth made the neuronal application, Miesenböck proposed early genetically targeted photoactivation. Six names cannot all be honoured; my trio is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a tool with thousands of independent applications; clinical translation (e.g. vision restoration) is early.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six candidates is contested and cannot be resolved by the supplied data.
Impact is predominantly methodological rather than therapeutic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 discovery, human genetics (gain- and loss-of-function variants) and therapeutic targeting yielded a new class of LDL-lowering drugs with outcome benefit, a model for genetically validated drug targets.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel and Boileau identified gain-of-function mutations, Seidah characterized the proprotein convertase, Hobbs and Cohen showed loss-of-function protection. Five credited names exceed three laureate slots, and any trio omits foundational contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: approved antibodies and siRNA, outcome trials confirmed benefit. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation between the discoverers of disease mutations and those of protective variants is unresolved.
Incremental benefit relative to statins, and long-term safety, still matter to some assessors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing) with implications for secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. Original, conceptually clear basic discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the pivotal pair, with the supplied list limited to them, giving a clean configuration. Earlier contributions (Kozutsumi, Ron and others) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic science with broad confirmation; direct therapeutic validation is still emerging.
uncertainties: Medical translation remains modest compared with other candidates.
Roles of other pioneers of ER stress signalling are not represented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 identified as a survival rather than proliferation oncogene, defined the apoptosis regulatory network, and underpinned venetoclax therapy for leukaemia. Clear mechanistic and translational impact.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led cloning and functional characterization, Vaux showed the cooperation with myc and cell death regulation; Strasser contributed later work. Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer, important in early BCL-2 translocation work, are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature with decades of confirmation and approved BH3-mimetic therapy, though apoptosis was already recognized in 2002.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize on programmed cell death may reduce its novelty to committee members.
Absence of other early BCL-2 researchers complicates fair credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as the central controller of cell growth linking nutrients and growth factors to protein synthesis has major implications for metabolism, ageing, cancer and transplantation (rapamycin). Original and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined its function; Sabatini (and Schreiber's group) identified mammalian mTOR and its partners. Schreiber's role in FRAP/mTOR is substantial but I limit to two for a cleaner configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic science and with clinical use of rapalogs, though mTOR-targeted therapy results in cancer and ageing are mixed.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and Brown or Abraham is contested.
Therapeutic impact beyond transplantation and some cancers is incomplete.
